event.summary: Separate exit, daemon, and rootless-sweep oracles cover the removed automatic cleanup test
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. Synthesis conclusion: do not report the absence of a combined automatic-exit-plus-daemon test as a missing cleanup mechanism. Original potential consequence retained: a broken host-exit notifier or real descendant cleanup could escape tests after deletion of the tmux integration tests. The source and distinguishing oracles are: (1) crates/farhelm/tests/e2e/host_tabs.rs:521–565 serves a supervisor at a 600-second interval, opens a real tab, types exit, and requires not only its listing empty but also host process gone and socket/record removed. Listing alone could pass without any reap; these other oracles require the event-driven automatic close. (2) core.rs:13937–14059 routes explicit close(false) and try_close_tab(true) through the same close_tab_claimed, close_tab_under_claim and close_host_tab_under_claim. host_tabs.rs:964–1040 branches on only_if_dead solely to recheck reap_due and log; all cleanup, host ending, survivor sweep and record removal then share identical code. core.rs:14120–14180 converts a dead/gone child to no root and passes the same tab target to the same reaper. (3) terminal_tabs.rs:307–345 creates a double-forked setsid descendant that ignores HUP before publishing its PID; :619–666 waits for that PID, explicitly closes its tab, requires daemon and shell gone, and requires a second tab and agent still answer. The marked shell cannot provide a PPID route to a reparented daemon, and terminal hangup cannot kill this HUP-immune daemon. This test demonstrates real descendant cleanup and isolation, but does not isolate scope from marker selection: harness.rs:1793–1795, :1956–1973 and core.rs:1150–1166 use the default systemd scope manager. That corrects and narrows my earlier implication that its result proves marker scanning alone. (4) sweep.rs:3366–3423, a_sigterm_ignoring_tab_process_ends_by_hangup_inside_the_grace, calls kill_process_tree_with_grace(None, session, SweepTarget::Tab, grace) on a real marked sleeper. There is no explicit root and no scope call in that entry point. It requires the tab sleeper's exit signal to be SIGHUP and the separately session-marked agent still alive. Thus it distinguishes rootless tab-marker selection and signal delivery from scope cleanup, a child-root PPID walk, or a whole-session overreach. sweep.rs:587–629 inserts marked identities before optional roots and expands the same closure regardless of root presence. This provides the missing rootless-marker oracle independently of the explicit close test. Contract: SPEC.md Session view requires exited tabs reaped automatically and their processes cleaned; SPEC_impl.md Terminal host/Tabs in hosts specifies notifier-driven reap and survivor sweep. These are source/test-contract checks only; no tests were executed. No unmarked-shell premise is established or claimed by any of these citations. They do not refute g103/f1, which concerns a distinct unmarked-shell/descendant-root coverage claim. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage candidate only); confidence: confirmed source-based refutation of this narrowly stated missing-mechanism concern; could-be-highest: no established shipped security or loss-of-work route. proposed_drop: source refutation through actual shared dispatch plus distinct automatic-close, real-daemon and rootless-marker oracles above; not acceptance based on correct production code alone. possible_cover: none. No unresolved premise remains for l1.
